notes: OWASP Juice Shop is a deliberately-vulnerable Node.js web app
shipped by OWASP for DAST training. Running ZAP baseline against
it reliably surfaces a known set of HTTP-layer alerts (CSP,
cross-origin, dangerous JS function calls, etc.) — the recall
check below requires secscan to detect each one.
Match logic: secscan Finding.rule_id == ZAP pluginid. A fixture
entry counts as detected when at least one secscan finding has
that pluginid. The set below is the stable baseline observed
with zap-baseline against juice-shop v17.0.0; if Juice Shop
rolls forward or ZAP's plugin IDs change, regenerate the set
via a manual ``secscan dast`` run and update this file.

expected_findings.name: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set

expected_active_findings.name: Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
expected_active_findings.note: fires in both baseline and active

expected_active_findings.name: Backup File Disclosure
expected_active_findings.cwe_topic: CWE-538: File and Directory Information Exposure

expected_active_findings.name: Bypassing 403 (auth bypass)
expected_active_findings.note: active-only: classic CWE-287 detection — sends status-manipulation payloads to reach 403-protected paths. This is what the baseline-vs-active comparison is for.
